subject: FAR
title: Error Correction Worksheet: Inventory, Capitalization, and Accruals
scenario:
Meridian Industrial Supply Co. is a calendar-year manufacturer. In February Year 3, before the Year 2 books were closed and before the Year 2 financial statements were issued, the company's newly hired controller completed a review of the accounting records and identified several errors affecting Year 1 and Year 2.

Selected financial data as currently reported are presented in **Exhibit 1**. The controller's findings are described in **Exhibit 2**. Accounting policies and other information appear in **Exhibit 3**.

For all tasks, ignore income tax effects.

exhibits.title: Exhibit 1: Selected Financial Data (As Currently Reported)
exhibits.content:
| Item | Year 1 | Year 2 |
|---|---|---|
| Net sales | $3,100,000 | $3,400,000 |
| Net income (Year 2 amount is preliminary; books not yet closed) | $500,000 | $620,000 |
| Dividends declared and paid | $100,000 | $120,000 |
| Total assets at December 31 | $2,900,000 | $3,150,000 |

Retained earnings at January 1, Year 1 (as previously reported): **$800,000**

exhibits.title: Exhibit 2: Controller's Findings
exhibits.content:
**Finding 1.** The physical inventory count at December 31, Year 1 included $40,000 of goods held on consignment from Apex Materials Inc. (Meridian is the consignee and never held title to the goods). No purchase was recorded for these goods. As a result, ending inventory at December 31, Year 1 was overstated by $40,000. The December 31, Year 2 count correctly excluded all consigned goods.

**Finding 2.** Goods costing $25,000, shipped by a vendor FOB shipping point on December 28, Year 2 and received on January 4, Year 3, were excluded from the December 31, Year 2 physical inventory count. The related purchase was correctly recorded in December Year 2. Ending inventory at December 31, Year 2 was therefore understated by $25,000.

**Finding 3.** On January 2, Year 1, Meridian paid $60,000 for a stamping machine and charged the entire amount to repairs and maintenance expense. The machine has an estimated useful life of 5 years and no salvage value. No depreciation has been recorded on this machine in Year 1 or Year 2.

**Finding 4.** Salaries earned by employees during the last week of December Year 2, totaling $18,000, were not accrued at December 31, Year 2. The salaries were paid and charged to expense on January 8, Year 3. Salaries were properly accrued at December 31, Year 1.

**Finding 5.** On January 2, Year 2, Meridian purchased a packaging machine for $90,000 (estimated salvage value $10,000; estimated useful life 10 years) and correctly capitalized the cost. The bookkeeper recorded Year 2 depreciation of $9,000, computed by ignoring the salvage value.

exhibits.title: Exhibit 3: Accounting Policies and Other Information
exhibits.content:
- Depreciation policy: straight-line method; a full year of depreciation is recorded in the year of acquisition.
- Meridian uses a periodic inventory system; cost of goods sold is determined from the year-end physical count.
- On July 1, Year 2, Meridian renewed a three-year product liability insurance policy for $36,000. The premium was recorded as prepaid insurance and is being amortized ratably over the coverage period; the controller verified that this policy was recorded correctly.
- Meridian maintains a $500,000 revolving line of credit bearing interest at 7%; no amounts were drawn during Year 1 or Year 2.
- The Year 1 financial statements will be presented for comparative purposes with the Year 2 financial statements.

tasks.title: Counterbalancing Effect of the Inventory Error
tasks.instruction: Assume Finding 1 (the $40,000 overstatement of December 31, Year 1 inventory) had never been discovered and no correction was ever made. What would be the effect of this error on retained earnings at December 31, Year 2, after the Year 2 closing entries?
options: No effect; the error counterbalances (self-corrects) over the two-year period
Retained earnings would be overstated by $40,000
Retained earnings would be understated by $40,000
Retained earnings would be overstated by $80,000
tasks.correctAnswer: No effect; the error counterbalances (self-corrects) over the two-year period
tasks.explanation: An ending inventory error counterbalances over two accounting periods. The $40,000 overstatement of December 31, Year 1 inventory understated Year 1 cost of goods sold, overstating Year 1 net income by $40,000. Because Year 1 ending inventory becomes Year 2 beginning inventory, Year 2 cost of goods sold was overstated, understating Year 2 net income by $40,000. After the Year 2 closing entries, the two effects offset exactly, so retained earnings at December 31, Year 2 is correctly stated. The individual-year income statements (and comparative statements, if presented) would still be misstated.
tasks.explanationJa:
期末棚卸資産の誤謬は**2期間でカウンターバランス（自動相殺）**します。

1. Year 1 期末棚卸資産が $40,000 過大 → Year 1 の売上原価が $40,000 過小 → **Year 1 純利益が $40,000 過大**
2. Year 1 期末在庫は Year 2 期首在庫になるため、Year 2 の売上原価が $40,000 過大 → **Year 2 純利益が $40,000 過小**
3. Year 2 の締切後、両者は完全に相殺されるため、**Year 2 末の利益剰余金への影響はゼロ**

ただし各年度の純利益（および比較財務諸表）は依然として誤表示のままである点に注意してください。

tasks.title: Error Correction Worksheet
tasks.instruction: For each finding in **Exhibit 2**, enter the amount by which the net income currently computed for each year should be increased or decreased to correct the error. Enter increases as positive numbers and decreases as negative numbers (e.g., enter -5000 if the reported net income should be reduced by $5,000). Enter 0 in any cell where the finding has no effect on that year. Whole dollars, no commas. Ignore income taxes.

rows: Finding 1: Consigned goods in Year 1 ending inventory
Finding 2: In-transit goods omitted from Year 2 ending inventory
Finding 3: Equipment charged to repairs expense
Finding 4: Unaccrued salaries at December 31, Year 2
Finding 5: Depreciation on Year 2 machine purchase

tasks.explanation: Finding 1: Year 1 ending inventory overstated by $40,000 understated Year 1 cost of goods sold, so Year 1 net income must be decreased by $40,000. The same misstated balance is Year 2 beginning inventory, which overstated Year 2 cost of goods sold, so Year 2 net income must be increased by $40,000. Finding 2: Year 2 ending inventory was understated by $25,000 while the purchase was recorded, so Year 2 cost of goods sold was overstated; increase Year 2 net income by $25,000 (no Year 1 effect). Finding 3: Year 1 expenses included $60,000 that should have been capitalized; correct Year 1 depreciation is $60,000 / 5 = $12,000, so Year 1 expenses were overstated by a net $48,000 (increase Year 1 net income by $48,000). Year 2 is missing $12,000 of depreciation (decrease Year 2 net income by $12,000). Finding 4: $18,000 of Year 2 salaries expense was omitted; decrease Year 2 net income by $18,000. Finding 5: Correct depreciation is ($90,000 - $10,000) / 10 = $8,000, but $9,000 was recorded, so Year 2 expense was overstated by $1,000; increase Year 2 net income by $1,000. Column totals: Year 1 +$8,000; Year 2 +$36,000.
tasks.explanationJa:
各誤謬の影響を修正額（＋＝利益を増やす、−＝利益を減らす）で整理します。

**Finding 1（Year 1 期末在庫 $40,000 過大）**
- Year 1: 売上原価が過小 → 利益が過大 → 修正 **−$40,000**
- Year 2: 期首在庫が過大 → 売上原価が過大 → 利益が過小 → 修正 **＋$40,000**

**Finding 2（Year 2 期末在庫 $25,000 過小、仕入は計上済み）**
- Year 2: 売上原価が過大 → 修正 **＋$25,000**（Year 1 は影響なし）

**Finding 3（設備 $60,000 を修繕費として費用処理）**
- Year 1: 本来は資産計上し減価償却 $60,000 ÷ 5年 = $12,000 のみ費用化すべき → 費用が正味 $48,000 過大 → 修正 **＋$48,000**
- Year 2: 減価償却費 $12,000 が未計上 → 修正 **−$12,000**

**Finding 4（Year 2 末の未払給与 $18,000 未計上）**
- Year 2: 費用が過小 → 修正 **−$18,000**

**Finding 5（Year 2 の減価償却計算誤り）**
- 正しい償却費 = ($90,000 − $10,000) ÷ 10年 = $8,000。計上額は $9,000 → 費用が $1,000 過大 → 修正 **＋$1,000**

**列合計**: Year 1 = ＋$8,000、Year 2 = ＋$36,000

tasks.title: Corrected Year 1 Net Income
tasks.instruction: Compute the corrected net income for Year 1 (in whole dollars, no commas). Ignore income taxes.
tasks.explanation: Corrected Year 1 net income = $500,000 as reported - $40,000 (inventory overstatement, Finding 1) + $48,000 (equipment expensed net of $12,000 depreciation, Finding 3) = $508,000. Findings 2, 4, and 5 do not affect Year 1.
tasks.explanationJa:
訂正後 Year 1 純利益の計算:

| 項目 | 金額 |
|---|---|
| 報告済み Year 1 純利益 | $500,000 |
| Finding 1: 期末在庫過大 | −$40,000 |
| Finding 3: 費用処理した設備（$60,000 − 償却 $12,000） | ＋$48,000 |
| **訂正後 Year 1 純利益** | **$508,000** |

Finding 2・4・5 は Year 2 のみに影響するため、Year 1 には影響しません。

tasks.title: Corrected Year 2 Net Income
tasks.instruction: Compute the corrected net income for Year 2 (in whole dollars, no commas). Ignore income taxes.
tasks.explanation: Corrected Year 2 net income = $620,000 preliminary + $40,000 (Finding 1 counterbalance) + $25,000 (Finding 2) - $12,000 (Finding 3 depreciation) - $18,000 (Finding 4 salaries) + $1,000 (Finding 5 depreciation overstatement) = $620,000 + $36,000 = $656,000.
tasks.explanationJa:
訂正後 Year 2 純利益の計算:

| 項目 | 金額 |
|---|---|
| 暫定 Year 2 純利益 | $620,000 |
| Finding 1: 期首在庫過大（カウンターバランス） | ＋$40,000 |
| Finding 2: 期末在庫過小 | ＋$25,000 |
| Finding 3: 減価償却費の計上漏れ | −$12,000 |
| Finding 4: 未払給与の計上漏れ | −$18,000 |
| Finding 5: 減価償却費の過大計上 | ＋$1,000 |
| **訂正後 Year 2 純利益** | **$656,000** |

修正合計 = ＋$36,000（Work Tab 2 の Year 2 列合計と一致）

tasks.title: Corrected Retained Earnings at December 31, Year 2
tasks.instruction: Using the corrected net income amounts and the dividend information in **Exhibit 1**, compute the corrected retained earnings balance at December 31, Year 2 (in whole dollars, no commas). Ignore income taxes.
tasks.explanation: Corrected retained earnings, December 31, Year 2 = $800,000 (January 1, Year 1 balance) + $508,000 (corrected Year 1 net income) - $100,000 (Year 1 dividends) + $656,000 (corrected Year 2 net income) - $120,000 (Year 2 dividends) = $1,744,000. Check: retained earnings as currently computed = $800,000 + $500,000 - $100,000 + $620,000 - $120,000 = $1,700,000; cumulative correction = $8,000 + $36,000 = $44,000; $1,700,000 + $44,000 = $1,744,000.

tasks.title: Classification: Error vs. Change in Principle vs. Change in Estimate
tasks.instruction: Which of the following items are accounted for as a correction of an error (prior-period adjustment with restatement of prior periods presented) under ASC 250? Select all that apply.
options: Failure to accrue salaries earned but unpaid at year end
Recording the cost of a machine as repairs and maintenance expense
A change from the FIFO cost flow method to the weighted-average cost method
A revision of a machine's estimated useful life from 10 years to 6 years based on new usage information
A change in the estimated salvage value of a fleet of delivery trucks
A change from the cash basis of accounting to the accrual basis of accounting
correctAnswer: Failure to accrue salaries earned but unpaid at year end
Recording the cost of a machine as repairs and maintenance expense
A change from the cash basis of accounting to the accrual basis of accounting
tasks.explanation: Corrections of errors result from mathematical mistakes, mistakes in applying GAAP, or oversight or misuse of facts that existed when the statements were prepared. Failing to accrue salaries and expensing a machine that should have been capitalized are both misapplications of GAAP, corrected by restatement. A change from the cash basis to the accrual basis is also a correction of an error because the cash basis is not GAAP. In contrast, a change from FIFO to weighted-average cost is a change in accounting principle (applied retrospectively, but it is not an error correction), and revisions of useful life or salvage value are changes in accounting estimate, accounted for prospectively.
tasks.explanationJa:
ASC 250 の3分類を整理します。

**誤謬の訂正（restatement / 期首RE修正）**
- 未払給与の計上漏れ → GAAP適用の誤り = **誤謬**
- 機械の取得原価を修繕費として費用処理 → GAAP適用の誤り = **誤謬**
- 現金主義から発生主義への変更 → 現金主義は**そもそもGAAPではない**ため、GAAPへの変更は**誤謬の訂正**として扱う（頻出のひっかけ）

**会計方針の変更（遡及適用だが誤謬ではない）**
- FIFO → 加重平均法への変更

**会計上の見積りの変更（将来に向かって処理）**
- 耐用年数の変更（10年 → 6年）
- 残存価額の見積り変更

tasks.title: Correcting Journal Entry for the Equipment Error
tasks.instruction: Prepare the journal entry at December 31, Year 2 to correct Finding 3 (the stamping machine charged to repairs and maintenance expense), assuming the Year 2 books have not been closed and no Year 2 depreciation has yet been recorded on this machine. Ignore income taxes. Enter amounts in whole dollars, no commas. Enter 0 in cells that should have no amount.
tasks.explanation: Debit Equipment $60,000 to record the asset. Credit Retained earnings $48,000 for the prior-period adjustment: Year 1 net income was understated by $60,000 (expense overstatement) less $12,000 (Year 1 depreciation that should have been recorded) = $48,000. Debit Depreciation expense $12,000 for the current-year (Year 2) depreciation, since the Year 2 books are still open. Credit Accumulated depreciation $24,000 for two years of depreciation ($12,000 x 2). Debits $72,000 = Credits $72,000.
tasks.explanationJa:
Year 2 の帳簿が未締切のため、Year 2 分の減価償却費は当期費用として計上し、Year 1 分の影響は利益剰余金（期首修正）で処理します。

| 勘定科目 | 借方 | 貸方 |
|---|---|---|
| 設備（Equipment） | $60,000 | |
| 減価償却費（Year 2 分） | $12,000 | |
| 減価償却累計額（2年分 = $12,000 × 2） | | $24,000 |
| 利益剰余金（Year 1 過小利益 $60,000 − $12,000） | | $48,000 |

- 資産計上漏れ: 借方 Equipment $60,000
- Year 1 の純利益過小額 = 費用過大 $60,000 − 未計上償却費 $12,000 = **$48,000** → 貸方 RE
- Year 2 の償却費 $12,000 は帳簿未締切のため当期の費用へ
- 借方合計 $72,000 = 貸方合計 $72,000 で貸借一致

subject: FAR
title: Accounting Change, Change in Estimate, and Correction of Prior Period Errors
scenario:
Calder Manufacturing Company is preparing its December 31, Year 3 comparative financial statements, which will present Year 3 and Year 2. Before recording any of the matters described below, the company's accountant prepared the preliminary amounts shown in **Exhibit 1**.

Effective January 1, Year 3, Calder changed its inventory costing method. Data supporting the change is presented in **Exhibit 2**. During the year-end closing process the company also identified matters relating to two long-lived assets, summarized in **Exhibit 3**, and two additional items, summarized in **Exhibit 4**.

All amounts are material. The company applies each accounting change and error correction in accordance with U.S. GAAP. Ignore income taxes and round all amounts to the nearest whole dollar.

exhibits.title: Exhibit 1: Preliminary Amounts Before Any Adjustments
exhibits.content:
| Item | Amount |
| --- | --- |
| Retained earnings, January 1, Year 3, as previously reported | $2,450,000 |
| Net income for Year 3, as preliminarily computed | 610,000 |
| Net income for Year 2, as previously reported | 520,000 |
| Dividends declared during Year 3 | 150,000 |
| Dividends declared during Year 2 | 120,000 |

The preliminary Year 3 net income was computed using the weighted-average inventory costing method described in Exhibit 2 and includes depreciation of $90,000 on the equipment described in Exhibit 3. It includes no depreciation on the machine described in Exhibit 3.

exhibits.title: Exhibit 2: Change in Inventory Costing Method
exhibits.content:
Effective January 1, Year 3, Calder changed from the first-in, first-out (FIFO) method to the weighted-average method of costing inventory. Management concluded that the weighted-average method is preferable and that the effects of the change can be determined for all prior periods presented.

| Inventory balance | FIFO | Weighted average |
| --- | --- | --- |
| December 31, Year 1 | $700,000 | $655,000 |
| December 31, Year 2 | 820,000 | 760,000 |
| December 31, Year 3 | Not determined | 905,000 |

There was no inventory on hand before December 31, Year 1 that had not been sold by that date, and no inventory write-downs were required in any year.

exhibits.title: Exhibit 3: Long-Lived Assets
exhibits.content:
**Machine.** A machine was purchased and placed in service on January 1, Year 2 at a cost of $480,000. The machine has an eight-year useful life and no residual value, and the company uses the straight-line method. The purchase was correctly capitalized, but no depreciation on the machine has ever been recorded in any year, including Year 3.

**Equipment.** Equipment was purchased and placed in service on January 1, Year 1 at a cost of $900,000. It was originally assigned a ten-year useful life with no residual value, and depreciation was correctly recorded on a straight-line basis in Year 1 and Year 2. On January 1, Year 3, based on the manufacturer's revised guidance and the company's operating experience, management revised the total useful life of the equipment to seven years from the date of purchase and estimated a residual value of $40,000. Depreciation of $90,000 on this equipment was recorded in the preliminary Year 3 amounts using the original estimates.

exhibits.title: Exhibit 4: Other Items Identified
exhibits.content:
**Insurance.** On July 1, Year 2, Calder paid $72,000 for a two-year insurance policy covering the period July 1, Year 2 through June 30, Year 4. The entire $72,000 was charged to insurance expense in Year 2, and no insurance expense relating to this policy has been recorded in the preliminary Year 3 amounts. The policy provides coverage evenly over its term.

**Wages.** Wages of $28,000 earned by employees during the last week of December Year 2 were not accrued at December 31, Year 2. The wages were paid on January 5, Year 3 and were charged to wages expense in the preliminary Year 3 amounts.

tasks.title: Cumulative Effect of the Inventory Method Change
tasks.instruction: Determine the cumulative effect of the change in inventory costing method on the retained earnings balance at January 1, Year 3. Enter the amount in whole dollars, no commas, and enter a decrease as a negative number.
tasks.explanation: The cumulative effect equals the difference in the inventory balance at the beginning of Year 3, that is, at December 31, Year 2: $760,000 - $820,000 = -$60,000. Lower inventory means higher cumulative cost of goods sold, so retained earnings decreases by $60,000.
tasks.explanationJa:
会計方針の変更は遡及適用され、累積的影響額は変更後の期首利益剰余金に反映される。

1. 累積的影響額は Year 3 期首（= Year 2年12月31日）の棚卸資産の差額で測る
2. 加重平均法 $760,000 - FIFO $820,000 = **△$60,000**
3. 棚卸資産が減る＝累積の売上原価が増えるため、期首利益剰余金は $60,000 減少する

Year 3期首残高の調整であるため、Year 3の当期純利益には影響しない（Year 3の暫定値は既に加重平均法で算定されている）。

tasks.title: Restated Year 2 Net Income
tasks.instruction: Determine the Year 2 net income as it should be presented in the Year 3 comparative financial statements. Enter the amount in whole dollars, no commas.
tasks.explanation: Start with $520,000 as previously reported. The inventory method change reduces Year 2 income by ($60,000) - ($45,000) = $15,000. The omitted machine depreciation of $480,000 / 8 = $60,000 reduces income. The insurance premium overcharged to Year 2 of $72,000 - ($3,000 x 6) = $54,000 increases income. The unaccrued wages of $28,000 reduce income. Restated Year 2 net income = $520,000 - $15,000 - $60,000 + $54,000 - $28,000 = $471,000.
tasks.explanationJa:
比較財務諸表の Year 2 は、方針変更の遡及適用と誤謬の訂正の両方を反映して修正再表示する。

1. 従来報告の Year 2 純利益 $520,000
2. 棚卸資産の方針変更: 期末差額 △60,000 - 期首差額 △45,000 = **△$15,000**
3. 機械の減価償却の計上漏れ: 480,000 ÷ 8年 = **△$60,000**
4. 保険料の過大計上: 72,000 - (72,000 ÷ 24か月 × 6か月 = 18,000) = **+$54,000**
5. 未払賃金の計上漏れ: **△$28,000**
6. 修正後 = 520,000 - 15,000 - 60,000 + 54,000 - 28,000 = **$471,000**

設備の見積り変更は将来にわたる処理なので、Year 2 は修正しない。

tasks.title: Adjusted January 1, Year 3 Retained Earnings
tasks.instruction: Determine the retained earnings balance at January 1, Year 3 after all required adjustments. Enter the amount in whole dollars, no commas.
tasks.explanation: Beginning with $2,450,000 as previously reported: subtract the $60,000 cumulative effect of the inventory method change, subtract the $60,000 of machine depreciation omitted in Year 2, add the $54,000 of insurance that benefits later periods, and subtract the $28,000 of unaccrued wages. The adjusted balance is $2,356,000.
tasks.explanationJa:
Year 3 期首利益剰余金を、方針変更の累積的影響と過年度誤謬の訂正で調整する。

1. 従来報告の期首残高 $2,450,000
2. 棚卸資産の方針変更の累積的影響 **△$60,000**
3. 機械の Year 2 減価償却の計上漏れ **△$60,000**
4. Year 2末時点で前払いとなっている保険料 **+$54,000**（$3,000/月 × 18か月分は Year 3以降の費用）
5. 未払賃金の計上漏れ **△$28,000**
6. 調整後 = 2,450,000 - 60,000 - 60,000 + 54,000 - 28,000 = **$2,356,000**

設備の見積り変更（将来処理）と Year 3 の配当は期首残高に影響しない。

tasks.title: Revised Depreciation on the Equipment
tasks.instruction: Determine the depreciation expense on the equipment for Year 3 after giving effect to the revised useful life and residual value. Enter the amount in whole dollars, no commas.
tasks.explanation: Original annual depreciation was $900,000 / 10 = $90,000, so accumulated depreciation at January 1, Year 3 was $180,000 and the carrying amount was $720,000. The revised total life of seven years leaves five years remaining. Revised depreciation = ($720,000 - $40,000) / 5 = $136,000.
tasks.explanationJa:
会計上の見積りの変更は**将来にわたって**処理し、過年度は修正しない。

1. 当初の年間減価償却費 = 900,000 ÷ 10年 = $90,000
2. Year 1・Year 2 の減価償却累計額 = 90,000 × 2年 = $180,000
3. Year 3期首の帳簿価額 = 900,000 - 180,000 = **$720,000**
4. 改定後の総耐用年数7年 - 経過2年 = **残存耐用年数5年**
5. Year 3 の減価償却費 = (720,000 - 40,000) ÷ 5年 = **$136,000**

暫定値には$90,000が計上済みなので、追加で$46,000を計上する必要がある。

tasks.title: Adjusted Year 3 Net Income
tasks.instruction: Determine the Year 3 net income after all required adjustments. Enter the amount in whole dollars, no commas.
tasks.explanation: Start with the preliminary $610,000. Record the machine's Year 3 depreciation of $60,000. Record the additional equipment depreciation of $136,000 - $90,000 = $46,000. Record the Year 3 insurance expense of $3,000 x 12 = $36,000. Remove the $28,000 of December Year 2 wages that were charged to Year 3. Adjusted Year 3 net income = $610,000 - $60,000 - $46,000 - $36,000 + $28,000 = $496,000.
tasks.explanationJa:
Year 3 の暫定純利益に、当期に帰属すべき費用の追加・除外を反映する。

1. 暫定純利益 $610,000
2. 機械の Year 3 減価償却費 **△$60,000**（480,000 ÷ 8年）
3. 設備の追加減価償却費 **△$46,000**（136,000 - 既計上90,000）
4. Year 3 の保険料 **△$36,000**（$3,000/月 × 12か月）
5. Year 2 に帰属する賃金が Year 3 の費用になっている分の戻し **+$28,000**
6. 調整後 = 610,000 - 60,000 - 46,000 - 36,000 + 28,000 = **$496,000**

棚卸資産の方針変更は Year 3 の暫定値に既に反映済みのため、ここでの追加調整はない。

tasks.title: Treatment of the Revised Useful Life and Residual Value
tasks.instruction: Select how the revision of the equipment's useful life and residual value is accounted for.
options: Prospectively, by allocating the remaining carrying amount less the new residual value over the remaining useful life
Retrospectively, by restating the Year 1 and Year 2 comparative financial statements
As a prior period adjustment to the January 1, Year 3 retained earnings balance
As a separate cumulative-effect line item reported in Year 3 income
tasks.correctAnswer: Prospectively, by allocating the remaining carrying amount less the new residual value over the remaining useful life
tasks.explanation: A change in the estimated useful life or residual value of a depreciable asset is a change in accounting estimate. It is accounted for in the period of change and future periods, with no restatement of prior periods and no adjustment to opening retained earnings.
tasks.explanationJa:
耐用年数や残存価額の見直しは**会計上の見積りの変更**である。

見積りの変更は変更した期以降に将来にわたって処理し、過年度の財務諸表の修正再表示も期首利益剰余金の調整も行わない。また、累積的影響額を当期の損益に単独の項目として表示することもしない。

本問では Year 3期首の帳簿価額 $720,000 から新しい残存価額 $40,000 を控除し、残存耐用年数5年にわたって配分する。

tasks.title: Items Adjusting Opening Retained Earnings
tasks.instruction: Select every item below that requires an adjustment to the January 1, Year 3 retained earnings balance as previously reported.
options: The change from the FIFO method to the weighted-average method
The Year 2 depreciation on the machine that was never recorded
The revision of the equipment's useful life and residual value
The portion of the two-year insurance premium that benefits periods after December 31, Year 2
The accrued wages of $28,000 unrecorded at December 31, Year 2
The Year 3 depreciation on the machine acquired January 1, Year 2
correctAnswer: The change from the FIFO method to the weighted-average method
The Year 2 depreciation on the machine that was never recorded
The portion of the two-year insurance premium that benefits periods after December 31, Year 2
The accrued wages of $28,000 unrecorded at December 31, Year 2
tasks.explanation: A change in accounting principle applied retrospectively and the correction of errors affecting periods before Year 3 are both reflected in the opening balance of retained earnings. The revision of the equipment's estimates is applied prospectively, and the machine's Year 3 depreciation is a Year 3 expense, so neither affects the opening balance.
tasks.explanationJa:
期首利益剰余金を修正するのは、**遡及適用される方針変更**と**Year 3より前の期間に影響する誤謬**である。

**調整が必要**
- FIFOから加重平均法への変更（遡及適用の累積的影響 △60,000）
- Year 2 の機械の減価償却の計上漏れ（△60,000）
- 保険料のうち Year 2末時点で前払いとなっていた部分（+54,000）
- Year 2末の未払賃金の計上漏れ（△28,000）

**調整が不要**
- 設備の耐用年数・残存価額の見直し — 将来にわたる処理であり過年度に遡らない
- 機械の Year 3 分の減価償却 — Year 3 の費用であり期首残高には関係しない

subject: FAR
title: Correction of Prior Period Errors and Restatement
scenario:
Kestrel Industries, Inc. is preparing comparative financial statements for Year 2 and Year 3. Before the Year 3 financial statements were issued, the controller identified three errors that affected previously issued statements.

**Exhibit 1** presents amounts as previously reported. **Exhibit 2** describes the errors. Additional information appears in **Exhibit 3**.

Use the exhibits to complete the tasks below. Enter increases as positive numbers and decreases as negative numbers, in whole dollars. Ignore any effect on earnings per share.

exhibits.title: Exhibit 1: Amounts as Previously Reported
exhibits.content:
| Item | Year 1 | Year 2 | Year 3 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Net income | $400,000 | $520,000 | $610,000 (preliminary, before correction) |
| Dividends declared and paid | $80,000 | $100,000 | $120,000 |
| Retained earnings, end of year | $1,200,000 | $1,620,000 | Not yet determined |

The Year 3 net income of $610,000 is the preliminary amount computed before any of the errors in Exhibit 2 were corrected.

exhibits.title: Exhibit 2: Errors Identified
exhibits.content:
**Error 1 — Inventory count**

Ending inventory at December 31, Year 2 was overstated by $70,000 because of a counting error at one warehouse. Inventory at December 31, Year 1 and at December 31, Year 3 was counted and valued correctly.

**Error 2 — Insurance policy**

On January 2, Year 2, Kestrel paid $90,000 for a three-year property insurance policy covering Year 2, Year 3, and Year 4. The entire $90,000 was charged to insurance expense in Year 2. No insurance expense related to this policy was recorded in Year 3.

**Error 3 — Equipment**

On January 1, Year 2, Kestrel purchased specialized production equipment for $240,000 and charged the entire amount to repairs and maintenance expense. The equipment should have been capitalized and depreciated on a straight-line basis over an eight-year useful life with no salvage value. No depreciation was recorded on the equipment in Year 2 or Year 3. The equipment remained in service at December 31, Year 3.

exhibits.title: Exhibit 3: Additional Information
exhibits.content:
1. Kestrel's income tax rate is 21% for all years presented, and each of the three errors affects taxable income in the same period and by the same pretax amount as it affects book income.
2. Weighted average common shares outstanding were 500,000 in each year presented.
3. Comparative financial statements are presented for Year 2 and Year 3 only.
4. No errors were identified that originated in Year 1 or earlier.
5. The Year 3 financial statements had not been issued when the errors were identified.

tasks.title: Restated Year 2 net income
tasks.instruction: Determine Kestrel's restated net income for Year 2. Enter the amount in whole dollars, no commas.
tasks.explanation: Pretax effect on Year 2 = $(70,000) inventory + $60,000 insurance + $210,000 equipment = $200,000 increase. After tax = $200,000 x 79% = $158,000. Restated net income = $520,000 + $158,000 = $678,000.

tasks.title: Corrected Year 3 net income
tasks.instruction: Determine Kestrel's corrected net income for Year 3. Enter the amount in whole dollars, no commas.
tasks.explanation: Pretax effect on Year 3 = $70,000 inventory + $(30,000) insurance + $(30,000) depreciation = $10,000 increase. After tax = $10,000 x 79% = $7,900. Corrected net income = $610,000 + $7,900 = $617,900.
tasks.explanationJa:
Year 3 に影響する各誤謬の税前影響額を合算する。

| 誤謬 | 税前影響 | 計算 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 期首棚卸資産の過大計上 | +$70,000 | 売上原価が過大 → 利益が過少。修正で増加 |
| 保険料の未計上 | −$30,000 | Year 3 分 $30,000 の費用計上漏れ |
| 減価償却の未計上 | −$30,000 | $240,000 ÷ 8年 |
| **合計（税前）** | **+$10,000** | |

税引後: $10,000 × 0.79 = $7,900

修正後 Year 3 純利益 = $610,000 + $7,900 = **$617,900**

棚卸資産の誤謬は2期間で自動的に相殺される（Year 2 で −$70,000、Year 3 で +$70,000）点に注目する。

tasks.title: Adjustment to beginning retained earnings
tasks.instruction: Determine the adjustment to retained earnings as of January 1, Year 3 resulting from the correction of the errors. Enter an increase as a positive number and a decrease as a negative number, in whole dollars, no commas.
tasks.explanation: The cumulative after-tax effect of the errors on periods before Year 3 is the Year 2 effect of $158,000, because all three errors originated in Year 2.
tasks.explanationJa:
Jan 1, Year 3 時点の利益剰余金修正額は、Year 3 より前の期間に生じた誤謬の税引後累積影響額に等しい。

本問では3つの誤謬すべてが Year 2 に発生しているため、Year 2 の税引後影響額 $158,000 がそのまま修正額となる。

修正額 = **+$158,000**

これにより Dec 31, Year 2（= Jan 1, Year 3）の利益剰余金は $1,620,000 + $158,000 = $1,778,000 に修正再表示される。Year 1 以前に発生した誤謬はないため、Jan 1, Year 2 の期首残高 $1,200,000 は修正しない。

tasks.title: Restated retained earnings at December 31, Year 3
tasks.instruction: Determine the restated retained earnings balance at December 31, Year 3. Enter the amount in whole dollars, no commas.
tasks.explanation: Restated retained earnings at January 1, Year 3 = $1,620,000 + $158,000 = $1,778,000. Add corrected Year 3 net income of $617,900 and deduct Year 3 dividends of $120,000: $1,778,000 + $617,900 - $120,000 = $2,275,900.
tasks.explanationJa:
修正後の期首残高から利益剰余金をロールフォワードする。

| 項目 | 金額 |
| --- | --- |
| Dec 31, Year 2 の報告額 | $1,620,000 |
| 誤謬修正（税引後） | +$158,000 |
| 修正後 Jan 1, Year 3 残高 | $1,778,000 |
| Year 3 修正後純利益 | +$617,900 |
| Year 3 配当 | −$120,000 |
| **Dec 31, Year 3 残高** | **$2,275,900** |

配当は誤謬の影響を受けないため、報告額 $120,000 をそのまま用いる。

tasks.title: Pretax effect of each error by year
tasks.instruction: Determine the effect of each error on pretax income for Year 2 and Year 3, and the total for each year. Enter increases as positive numbers and decreases as negative numbers, in whole dollars, no commas.
tasks.explanation: Inventory: overstated Year 2 ending inventory understates Year 2 cost of goods sold and overstates Year 2 income by $70,000; the same overstatement becomes Year 3 beginning inventory, overstating Year 3 cost of goods sold by $70,000. Insurance: $90,000 was expensed in Year 2 instead of $30,000, so Year 2 expense was overstated by $60,000 and Year 3 expense was understated by $30,000. Equipment: $240,000 was expensed instead of recording $30,000 of depreciation, so Year 2 expense was overstated by $210,000, and Year 3 depreciation of $30,000 was omitted.
tasks.explanationJa:
各誤謬が両年度に与える税前影響を分解する。

| 誤謬 | Year 2 | Year 3 | 説明 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 棚卸資産 | −$70,000 | +$70,000 | 期末在庫過大 → Year 2 の売上原価過少・利益過大。翌期は期首在庫過大となり売上原価過大・利益過少 |
| 保険料 | +$60,000 | −$30,000 | Year 2 に $90,000 計上（正しくは $30,000）→ $60,000 の費用過大。Year 3 は $30,000 の計上漏れ |
| 設備 | +$210,000 | −$30,000 | $240,000 の費用過大から減価償却 $30,000 を差し引く。Year 3 は減価償却 $30,000 の計上漏れ |
| **合計** | **+$200,000** | **+$10,000** | |

棚卸資産の誤謬は「counterbalancing error」であり2期間で相殺されるが、保険料と設備の誤謬は複数期にわたって影響が残る。

tasks.title: Reporting the correction
tasks.instruction: Select how Kestrel reports the correction of these errors in its comparative Year 2 and Year 3 financial statements.
options: Restate the prior period financial statements presented and adjust the opening balance of retained earnings of the earliest period presented
Report the cumulative effect of the errors as a separate line item in Year 3 income before extraordinary items
Apply the correction prospectively beginning in Year 3 and disclose the nature of the errors
tasks.correctAnswer: Restate the prior period financial statements presented and adjust the opening balance of retained earnings of the earliest period presented
tasks.explanation: An error in previously issued financial statements is corrected by restating the prior period statements presented and adjusting the opening balance of retained earnings of the earliest period presented for the cumulative effect of errors that originated before that period, with disclosure of the nature of the error and its effect on each line item and per share amount.
tasks.explanationJa:
過年度の誤謬は、**遡及的な修正再表示（restatement）** によって処理する。

1. 比較表示される過年度の財務諸表を修正再表示する（本問では Year 2）
2. **表示される最も古い期間（earliest period presented）** の期首利益剰余金を、その期間より前に発生した誤謬の累積影響額だけ修正する
3. 誤謬の内容、各表示科目・1株当たり金額への影響を注記開示する

本問で表示される最も古い期間は Year 2 であり、3つの誤謬はいずれも Year 2 中に発生しているため、Jan 1, Year 2 の期首利益剰余金 $1,200,000 は結果として修正されない。仮に Year 1 以前に発生した誤謬があれば、その税引後累積影響額を Jan 1, Year 2 残高に反映することになる。

当期の損益に累積影響額を一括計上する方法や、将来に向かって適用する方法（prospective）は誤謬の修正には認められない。将来に向かっての適用は会計上の見積りの変更に用いる。

tasks.title: Research
tasks.instruction: Identify the authoritative guidance stating that an error in previously issued financial statements shall be reported as an error correction by restating the prior period financial statements. Cite the ASC reference in XXX-XX-XX-XX format.
tasks.explanation: ASC 250-10-45-23 requires that any error in the financial statements of a prior period discovered after the financial statements are issued or are available to be issued be reported as an error correction by restating the prior period financial statements.
tasks.explanationJa:
ASC 250-10-45-23 は、公表済み（または公表可能な状態にある）過年度財務諸表に誤謬が発見された場合、過年度財務諸表を修正再表示することにより誤謬の訂正として報告することを求めている。

同項はあわせて、修正再表示にあたり誤謬の影響を受ける資産・負債・利益剰余金の各期首残高を修正することも定めている。
